caption: A small snowball is set on a hot griddle, and it hisses and collapses into water and steam.

sa.check: A snowball is set on the griddle.
The snowball collapses: it loses its round shape and slumps.
Water spreads around it and steam rises.
The snowball is white and firm at the start.
The setting down comes first and the collapse follows.

pc.expect: The snowball only darkens, slumps and shrinks, and the wet patch around it only grows.
pc.fail: The snowball regains its round shape; or turns white and firm again on the griddle; or the wet patch draws back into the ball; or the ball alternates between firmer and softer.

pc.expect: The water and steam come from the snowball, which loses matter and gains none.
pc.fail: The snowball grows; or a second snowball appears; or the ball vanishes in a single frame while still round; or water appears across the griddle with none running there from the ball.

pc.expect: The ball settles downward as it slumps, the meltwater spreads outward across the griddle, and the steam rises.
pc.fail: The ball lifts off the griddle; or the meltwater climbs the griddle's edge and stays; or the steam sinks and pools around the griddle.

pc.expect: The snow collapses as a wet crumbling solid that slumps from the bottom where it meets the metal, and the melt is a thin film that sizzles.
pc.fail: The ball melts from its top while its underside stays white and dry; or the ball bends and flows as one soft lump; or the melt stands as a dome on the griddle; or the ball bounces on the metal.

pc.expect: The snowball sits on top of the griddle's surface and nothing passes through the metal.
pc.fail: The ball sinks into the griddle's metal; or the melt passes through the griddle; or the griddle changes shape; or a second griddle appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The griddle's finish and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The griddle changes colour; or its surface pattern changes; or items around it rearrange.
